findings.summary: list_ready calls onboarding_overlay_clause(&[]) instead of onboarding_overlay_clause(onboarding_libs), so the onboarding overlay clause is always empty in list_ready regardless of the caller's actual onboarding_libs — while the bind loop just below (line 388) still pushes one Value::Text per entry in the real onboarding_libs slice. Whenever any onboarding library is configured, the SQL has zero placeholders for those overlay binds but the bind vector still contains them, so rusqlite's positional binding either errors (parameter index out of range) or, depending on how many other `?` placeholders exist (library filter, LIMIT), silently misassigns an onboarding-library string to an unrelated placeholder (e.g. the LIMIT value), corrupting the query. This is exactly the drift the refactor was supposed to make impossible, contradicts the function's own doc comment (lines 350-351: 'the same onboarding overlay ... excludes onboarding_sample = 0 rows for onboarding_libs') and the brief's explicit 'pure refactor with no behavioral difference in the generated SQL' requirement. It breaks the operator-facing skip-scan dry-run/list path for any config with onboarding libraries.
